purpose: Assess an independently accessible Region II estuarine fishery study as an evidence lead, while preserving its site, date, sampling, taxonomy, and reuse limits. This is not a checklist or app-content approval.

sources.citation: Casco, C. B., Castro, M. R., Angeles Jr., I. P., Asprec, M. J. L., Ame, E. C., & Ballad, E. L. (2025). Catch Composition and Bycatch Species of Fyke Net from Glass Eel Fishery in Aparri, Cagayan, Philippines. Journal of Fisheries and Environment, 49(1), 22–34.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), as stated on the journal article page.

sources.citation: Escaño, V. M. C., Rey, J. T. S., Ame, E. C., Gaerlan, R. S., Tauli, M., Encarnacion, A. B., & Santos, M. D. (2022). Updates on Identification and Distribution of the River Mullet ‘Ludong’ in Northern Philippines. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 29(2), 139–148. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/29.2.2022A0003
sources.license: CC BY-NC 4.0, as stated on the final page of the article PDF.

cascoStudy.reportedStudySite: Fish landing site in Toran, Aparri, Cagayan, at the mouth of the Cagayan River.
cascoStudy.samplingUnit: Landed fyke-net catch from five glass-eel fishers.

identificationMethods.glassEels: Caudal pigmentation chart with microscope assistance.
identificationMethods.fishAndNonFishBycatch: Morphological identification using fish identification resources, including FishBase and SeaLifeBase.

sourceInternalChecks: The abstract reports 31 bycatch species in 16 families. A later results paragraph says 17 families and includes Anguillidae, which the paper also identifies as the target glass-eel family; retain the published wording and resolve the denominator before any derived count is reused.

Scientific-name spellings vary between the article's table and prose or between its two tables (for example, Amblygaster sirm and Cynoglossus bilineatus). Keep original source strings until checked independently against taxonomic authorities.
The article reports morphological IDs but the reviewed methods and species table provide no specimen-level voucher or sequence accessions.
spatialLimits: Toran is a landing site; a landed catch does not establish an exact capture point for every taxon.
The article includes a study-area figure but does not provide a reviewed point-coordinate dataset or a boundary suitable for mapping species occurrences.
The observations are from one gear and a March–April 2023 sampling window; they do not define a complete or current Aparri, Cagayan, Region II, or Philippine checklist.

nfrdiContext.finding: Escaño et al. report 25 retained CO1 sequences identified as Cestraeus goldiei; 24 samples are described from Cagayan River and tributaries across Cagayan and Isabela, with one Abra River sample.
nfrdiContext.disposition: Context only; the existing 2026 NFRDI/GenBank crosswalk already records 18 linked accessions and locality conflicts. This review does not add or geocode those samples again.
limitations: No coordinates are supplied by the article.
Paper locality text and linked GenBank province qualifiers conflict for four accessions, as documented in the existing crosswalk.
The paper's identification is a historical study result and not evidence of current presence or a complete ludong distribution.

reuseDisposition.cascoArticle: Journal terms identify CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Keep the downloaded copy in ignored research storage, cite the article, and do not reproduce or adapt its article/table content into app records without a separate rights review or permission.
reuseDisposition.nfrdiArticle: The article states CC BY-NC 4.0; existing source records and crosswalks are retained as provenance. This review does not approve app reuse.

nextAction: Prioritize separately licensed/open Region II river, lake, reservoir, lagoon, wetland, and estuary surveys. Independently validate candidate scientific names and site associations; do not treat this CC BY-NC-ND article's table as an app-ready dataset.
